classification.difficultyReason: Select a coefficient whose complementary indices become adjacent indices under binomial symmetry, then express the resulting binomial coefficient in factorial form.

content.prompt:
By considering $(1+x)^n(1+x)^n=(1+x)^{2n}$, equate an appropriate $x^r$ to show that
$$\binom n0\binom n1+\binom n1\binom n2+\binom n2\binom n3+\cdots+\binom n{n-1}\binom nn$$
is equal to $\displaystyle\frac{(2n)!}{(n-1)!(n+1)!}$.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle\frac{(2n)!}{(n-1)!(n+1)!}$.

Equate the coefficients of $x^{n-1}$ and use $\binom n{n-1-j}=\binom n{j+1}$.
